chunks: When they returned to him, they said (to Joseph): "O Minister, calamity has befallen us and our people. We have brought but a meagre sum, but give us full measure as alms bestowed. God surely rewards those who give alms."
ai.seo_question: What did Joseph's brothers say to him when they returned to Egypt to buy grain?
ai.summary: In this verse, Joseph’s brothers appeal to his sense of justice and charity, invoking the divine principle that God rewards those who give freely, a concept central to Shia ethical teachings on *sadaqah*. Their plea highlights the tension between their material need and their recognition of Joseph’s authority, setting the stage for his eventual revelation of identity. This moment underscores the Shia emphasis on patience (*sabr*) and divine providence in times of familial trial.
